method: Reviewer-maintained semantic fingerprints: thesis, reader task, evidence focus, and distinction from overlapping pieces; not a claim of unique facts or a cryptographic text hash.

semanticFingerprint.thesis: Delegating actions to an AI agent does not transfer organizational accountability: a named team must bound authority, explain consequential actions, and own escalation and repair.
semanticFingerprint.readerTask: Help leaders design ownership and response duties for AI-agent workflows after deployment.
semanticFingerprint.distinctFrom: Technical tool-permission comparisons and implementation checklists; this essay addresses accountability for outcomes and remedies.
semanticFingerprint.evidenceFocus: Agent oversight and permissions documentation plus security-control evidence, used to support an organizational argument rather than reproduce a control taxonomy.

articles.title: The word “small” is not a performance claim

semanticFingerprint.thesis: The word small is not a capability or deployment result by itself; readers need the model, task, hardware, memory, tool, and evaluation context behind the label.
semanticFingerprint.readerTask: Help readers interpret “small model” claims and identify what a public model release should disclose.
semanticFingerprint.distinctFrom: Hardware and workflow deployment guides, benchmark comparisons, and general model-card tutorials; this essay focuses on the meaning and disclosure of the size label.
semanticFingerprint.evidenceFocus: Provider model/system cards and bounded benchmark evidence, including the AgentFloor arXiv v1 submission; provider claims remain attributed and the preprint is not described as peer-reviewed proceedings.
